subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should this issue be resolved with latency-aware Slack docs/setup guidance for HTTP Request URLs, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and Slack recommends HTTP for deployed production apps, but changing the default setup path or stronger guidance affects operator requirements for public ingress, TLS, request signing, and multi-account webhook paths.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs toward HTTP mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the existing transport table is sufficient and close only after maintainers decide no additional latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the measurements, landed the partial channel-side fixes, and explicitly scoped the remaining HTTP-guidance work.
